I am an Economist at the Forecasting & Policy Modelling Division of DG Economics at the European Central Bank. I have five years of research experience in algorithms, game theory and mechanism design, and mathematical optimization, alongside three years of applied experience in data science and AI/ML engineering.
Before coming to the ECB, I was a postdoctoral researcher at the Department of Industrial Engineering of the University of Chile hosted by Prof. José Correa. I obtained my PhD from the Department of Mathematics of the TUM School of Computation, Information and Technology, where I was advised by Prof. Andreas S. Schulz and completed an interdisciplinary PhD program at the intersection of mathematics, computer science, and management science as a member of the research group AdONE. During my PhD and postdoc, I had the opportunity to spend some time at Google Research Zurich and the Sapienza University of Rome. I received my Diploma (BSc and MEng equivalent) in Electrical and Computer Engineering from the National Technical University of Athens, where I was advised by Prof. Dimitris Fotakis.
My research during my PhD and postdoc revolved mainly around the design of algorithms and mechanisms for fair and efficient resource allocation with applications in pricing, auctions, recommender systems, apportionment, and generally complex scenarios arising in (online) markets and platforms. I am now interested in the use of alternative data and the application of machine/deep learning techniques in macroeconomic forecasting.
You can find a copy of my CV here (last update: September 2026).
